description.p: Skribisto is a writing app for novels, from the first idea to the finished manuscript.
Skribisto est un logiciel d'écriture pour les romans, de la première idée au manuscrit terminé.

ul.li: Split panes and tabs, and a whole chapter, part or book readable as one text
Écran partagé et onglets, et un chapitre, une partie ou le livre entier à lire comme un seul texte
Corkboard, story bible, margin comments and footnotes
Tableau de liège, bible narrative, commentaires dans la marge et notes de bas de page
Word goals, writing sessions, pace planning and manuscript analysis
Objectifs de mots, sessions d'écriture, planification du rythme et analyse du manuscrit
Statuses you name yourself, from first draft to final
Des statuts que vous nommez vous-même, du premier jet à la version finale
Import from Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument or Markdown, comments included, with a report of anything left behind
Import depuis Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument ou Markdown, commentaires compris, avec un rapport de ce qui n'a pas pu être repris
Export to DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF and more, and finish the page layout in the program you prefer
Export en DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF et d'autres formats, pour finir la mise en page dans le logiciel de votre choix
Search and replace, autosave, backups and version history
Rechercher et remplacer, enregistrement automatique, sauvegardes et historique des versions
Spell checking, smart punctuation and 24 interface languages
Correcteur orthographique, ponctuation intelligente et interface en 24 langues
Built for accessibility: screen readers, braille displays and keyboard shortcuts
Pensé pour l'accessibilité : lecteurs d'écran, plages braille et raccourcis clavier

screenshot.caption: The binder and the editor, with prose and its synopsis side by side
Le classeur et l'éditeur, avec le texte et son synopsis côte à côte
The launcher, listing recent projects and bundled examples
Le lanceur, avec les projets récents et les exemples fournis

ul.li: Opening a text's menu with Shift+F10 or the Menu key leaves the cursor where it was. It used to jump to the middle of the text, so Paste landed there

Alt+Up and Alt+Down move the selected binder item up or down, and Alt+Down opens a list or a date field. Those keys used to go to the previous or next item from anywhere in the window; they now do that only while you write in a text

Go ▸ Next scene, Alt+Down and the other Go commands put the cursor in the text they open, so you can go on writing at once. It used to stay on the page you left, and a screen reader announced only the window

In the Help window, Enter on a topic, the Back button and a link to another page take you into the page's text, and a screen reader announces the page's title as its heading. Focus used to stay on the topic's button, with no sign that the page had changed

In Settings, Enter on a page in the list on the left, a link to a page, a page in the breadcrumb at the top or a search suggestion takes you to that page's first setting. Focus used to stay where it was, and was lost when that was on the page being left

Every on/off setting in Settings has its name on the left and its switch on the right, as most pages already did. Some pages put the switch first, and periodic backups now take two lines: one to turn them on, one for the interval

With a screen reader, the search fields in Settings, the binder, Search, the corkboard, the overview, Go to and the Launcher, the editable lines of the tags, statuses, templates, dictionary and text replacement pages, the fields that add a holiday or a milestone in Pace, and the bar of views at the top of a chapter, a part or a book now have names. They used to be announced with none, or by their grey hint until something was typed

Help ▸ Keyboard shortcuts opens Settings on its Keyboard shortcuts page, where every shortcut can be found and changed, in the Launcher too. It used to open a small sheet whose list the keyboard could not reach, and whose button did nothing in the Launcher. A Settings window opened for one page, from a message or a menu, now starts on that page's first setting
A screen reader announces the Help window as “Help - Skribisto” and each page by its title. They used to be “Skribisto” and an unnamed document

In the Help window, the short definitions under “What things are” open as pages you can enter and read with the keyboard, like the other topics. Their text used to be out of reach of Tab, and of Enter on the topic

With a screen reader, each line of the tags, statuses, note templates, dictionary and text replacement lists in Settings is announced by what it holds: the name of the tag, the status or the template, the word, or the shorthand and what it becomes. A tag used to be announced by its colour, a status by its number, and every word and every rule by the same field name
With a screen reader, the charts in Go back in time, in a book's Pace and in its Analysis are announced by their titles. They were announced in English, by how many series and categories they had

With a screen reader, the title, subtitle and chapter title fields above a text, and a note's name, are announced by name. They used to give only their grey hint, which disappears once they hold a name

Every panel has its own command and shortcut: Ctrl+Shift+B the binder, T the trash, C the comments, G the writing games, I the inspector, O formatting, D this document's comments, K the footnotes, R the versions, J the search preview and L Go back in time, beside Ctrl+Shift+F for Search. View ▸ Panels lists them all, and the command palette and Settings ▸ Keyboard shortcuts too

The View menu keeps the panels in their own submenu, then the left, right and bottom panels, then the window's modes. Panels and window settings used to be mixed in one list, and half the panels were missing from it

Search preview no longer claims F10, which belongs to the menu bar on Windows and Linux and never reached it there. Revealing an item in the binder brings the binder in front of Search or the Trash, which used to keep it hidden

Help ▸ Using a screen reader opens a new page for writers who use NVDA, JAWS, Orca or VoiceOver, with the cursor in its text: how the window is laid out, the shortcut of every panel, and the keys of the binder, the views bar, the menus and Settings

When Skribisto starts with a screen reader running, it offers to open that page. Tick “Do not show this again” to stop the offer; the page stays in the Help menu, and Settings ▸ Reset to defaults brings the offer back

Undo works again after a visit to Settings. Once Settings had been opened and closed, Ctrl+Z and Edit ▸ Undo no longer took back a move in the binder, a trash or any other change to the project's structure, for the rest of the session
Cut, Copy, Paste and Select all work in the fields of Settings and of the other dialogs, such as Rename. Ctrl+V and Ctrl+A did nothing there
A panel's shortcut, such as Ctrl+Shift+B for the binder, puts you in the panel, and a screen reader says its name. It used to bring the panel forward and leave the cursor where it was

F6 and Shift+F6 move between the left panels, the text in the centre and the right panels, and a screen reader says where you are. Tab goes through the window in reading order: the title bar, the left, the centre, the right and the status bar

With a screen reader, the binder says each item's level and its place among its neighbours, and Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens an item's own menu, with Move at the end. Every item used to read as level 1, and the keyboard opened a Move menu in English instead

With a screen reader, a menu command, a command palette row and a button say their keyboard shortcut. A menu opened from the keyboard starts on its first row, where it used to start on the row chosen last time
The Up and Down arrows change the view of a chapter, part or book, as Left and Right do

In Settings, the lines of the Tags, Statuses, Templates, Personal dictionary and Text replacements pages can be reached from the keyboard: F2 or Enter goes into a line, Tab moves between its fields and Escape comes back to the list
Tab leaves a synopsis, an epigraph, a comment and a footnote for the next control, as in any field. It typed a tab into them
In the help, Tab goes from link to link in a page and Enter follows one
A date field's calendar opens as a small dialog with Cancel and OK. Tab stays inside it, and a screen reader says the date chosen. Tab used to close the calendar without choosing
In New Work, Next takes you into the next page's first field and a screen reader announces the step. The cursor used to stay on Next
In a narrow window, the second half of a split editor no longer draws over the right panels: both halves shrink to fit
Enter at the end of a heading starts an ordinary paragraph, as in LibreOffice Writer, and Enter in the middle of one splits it

On Windows, input methods for Chinese, Japanese and Korean, the emoji panel and voice typing write into Skribisto as they do into Notepad: the candidate window follows the text, and voice typing shows its words as you speak
Chinese, Japanese and Korean text, and emoji, are drawn with the fonts your system uses for them, in colour for emoji, and bold or italic when the text around them is
After Add word, Add rule, Add tag or Add status in Settings, the cursor is back in the field, ready for the next one. It stayed on the button, which greys itself out once the field is empty
The Templates page of Settings fits a narrow window. Its row of buttons made it scroll sideways, cutting off the start of its lines

Ctrl+Shift+O puts you on the first button of the Format panel, like the other panels' shortcuts, and Tab moves through its buttons. They were out of reach of the keyboard, so the shortcut left you in the text. A click on one of them still leaves the cursor and the selection in the text

With a screen reader, the text of a scene, chapter or note is announced as “Text”, its synopsis as “Synopsis” (on a corkboard card too) and a chapter's epigraph as “Epigraph”, and the target box in the Inspector as “Target”. They used to be announced as edit fields with no name, so you could tell them apart only by reading the words in them

Undoing a change to the binder no longer erases what you wrote since. Undoing a move, a duplicate, a trash, a restore, Replace all or an import of tags or templates put the texts it covered back as they were before the change, so the words typed afterwards were lost and the open text was reloaded with a “Typing history reset” message. Only a text the change itself rewrote, as a merge, a split or Replace all does, goes back
When a chapter's Epigraph section is closed, Tab goes past it. It used to stop on its hidden Source line button and on its field
With a screen reader, the binder's items are no longer each described as a tooltip, the Rename field has a name, and a field whose grey hint repeats its name says that name only once

On Windows, a paragraph of the help is one paragraph for a screen reader, as in your own text, and with NVDA's Read by paragraph a braille display shows it whole. A hidden character at the end of each source line used to split it, and the display showed each of those lines as a paragraph of its own

Pictures show in the text again when a project is opened, a Scrivener project or a document is imported, or a text is reopened. Since version 3.0.5 they appeared as blank spaces of the right size, though they were safe in the project and present in exports. This includes macOS, and a high-resolution screen when the last project reopens at launch, where a picture could stay blank after the first fix

A picture added after a project was saved to a new place, with Save As or by the first save of a new folder project, shows when pasted into a text that was already open. It stayed a blank space until the project was closed

Bold, italic, headings and other formatting are saved with your project even if you type nothing afterwards. They used to stay in the open text and be gone the next time you opened the project. After an undo, Redo is offered straight away, and the Edit menu says “Undo the last change to this text”. It used to stay unavailable, and to call every change typing

When you import a project from Scrivener, Manuskript or Plume Creator, Skribisto suggests the folder you last chose for a new project, or your documents folder, instead of the folder your old project sits in. You can still choose any other folder, and Skribisto remembers it next time

Tabbing through a chapter no longer lands on an invisible button: the Tags control shows itself when you reach it, and Space opens it. Tags also show after opening a project from the Launcher, where their dots could be missing. In a column narrowed by the side panels, the corkboard and overview filters keep a field you can see and type in, and the cards stay inside the column. These filters used to shrink to almost nothing, and the cards were cut off at the edge

With a screen reader, Go ▸ Go to… (Ctrl+G) says how many items match as you type and the first of them, and the Up and Down arrows read each match with its place in the list. Enter opens the item with the cursor in its text. It used to say nothing about the results, and Enter left you on the window
Go to… also finds an untitled chapter by the name the binder gives it. It used to show the row, then skip it with the arrows and refuse to open it with Enter

F9 no longer leaves you on the window when the left panel hides with the cursor in it: the cursor goes to the text in the centre, or into the view in front of you when it has no text. A screen reader says when a left, right or bottom panel is hidden or shown, which it used not to. Leaving distraction-free mode with F11 puts the cursor back in your text

On the corkboard, Shift+F2 takes you into a card's synopsis from the keyboard, Tab goes round the card and Escape brings you back to it. A synopsis used to need the mouse, and once inside, Tab jumped to the title bar

On macOS, a project on a mounted remote drive, such as a WebDAV share, can now be saved and backed up. Every save used to fail with “fsyncing temp file” and left a hidden temporary file beside the project. A save is also no longer called failed when it reached the disk but macOS refuses access to its folder, which left the project marked unsaved

The panel names read out by a screen reader or listed under Keyboard shortcuts, the names of the title fields and a few other labels are now in your language in every translation. They used to appear in English in 22 of them

Entering distraction-free mode puts the cursor in your text where you left it, whichever way you enter, so you can go on writing at once. A page with no text takes the cursor in its view, and with nothing open the mode's bar takes it and a screen reader says there is nothing to type in. The cursor used to be lost: keys went nowhere, and a screen reader was left on nothing until you pressed Tab or left the mode. Also, a text in which the synopsis sits beside the prose keeps the cursor when the window gets too narrow or wide enough for that arrangement to change

After Work ▸ Save as folder… or Save as single file…, your recent works list the project where you saved it, at the top, and no longer offer the file you saved from. They used to keep only that older file, so reopening the project from the Launcher or the title bar opened a copy without anything written since. The older file stays where it was, and Work ▸ Open Work… still reaches it. The same goes for a backup you restore: the project it was put back into comes first

When your project cannot be saved as you quit, close it or open another one (a network drive that dropped, a full or write-protected disk, a USB key taken out), Skribisto now asks what to do: leave without saving, losing the changes since the last successful save, or Cancel to keep everything open and try again or use Save As. With autosave on, it used to stay open with only a message, so you could not quit without forcing it

A backup opened beside its project, or the file a Save As left behind opened beside the moved project, keeps its own count in Analysis ▸ Arrivals. The two windows used to add up into one count, kept even after both were closed

The Settings window grows with a larger interface text size, set in Settings or by your system. The list of pages on the left widens with it, and the bars at the top and bottom keep their margins. At 200 % it used to keep its usual size, so the names of the pages, the search field's hint and the commands under Keyboard shortcuts were cut short. Done now sits at the right end of the bottom bar, away from Reset to defaults

Dragging a chapter in the binder or a tab, and selecting text with the mouse, keep up with a fast mouse. With a 1000 Hz mouse on Linux they used to fall behind the pointer and finish only after the button was released
Copy and paste between Skribisto and other applications work on Linux under GNOME with Wayland, in the Flatpak too. They used to work only inside Skribisto there, with no message to say so

Undoing or redoing bold, italic, a heading or a list shows in the text at once, and counts as a change to save. The text used to keep its old look until you typed, and closing the project could lose the undo

In the text, on Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Right goes to the start of the next word, as in other editors, and Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down go to the start of a paragraph, with Shift to select. Ctrl+Right used to stop at the end of the word, and Ctrl+Up and Ctrl+Down moved one line

Left and Right with text selected go to the start or the end of the selection. They used to move one letter from the cursor, which could leave it inside the selection. On a line that wraps, Left no longer jumps from the second letter to the end of the line above, and after Undo, Redo, Backspace or Delete there the cursor stays on the line its text is on
The cursor stops blinking after ten seconds with nothing moving it, and stays shown. Typing, a click or coming back to the window starts the blink again

In a table, Down from the line above goes into its first row, Down from its last row goes to the text after it, and Up into a cell that wraps lands on its last line. Shift with an arrow inside a cell of several paragraphs selects text in that cell. The cursor used to stay where it was, or select whole cells

With a screen reader, a line break made with Shift+Enter is read as a line break, and an empty line between two of them as blank. On Windows, NVDA reads the line the cursor is on at the start of a wrapped line, where it used to read the line above. A braille routing key on the cell under the cursor no longer moves it a line up, and a braille display shows a list line at once after Backspace, Undo or Redo

In a message with Show details, such as the one asking what to do when a project cannot be saved, Enter on Show details shows them. It used to answer the question with the default button. Once shown, the details can be reached with Tab, read, selected and copied, and a message whose text wraps keeps its buttons inside it, where a click could miss them and count as Cancel
